title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Two past weeks with same or higher price increases saw sales drop 28% and 35% vs baseline; noise-adjusted effect shrunk toward 1.0 due to limited data.

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: New competitive threat; no direct past data, but consistent with demand loss in similar contexts; evidence is sparse, so effect shrunk.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. No events are scheduled, but a price increase to $4.56 (+5.1%) is in effect. Past data shows a 30% off promotion in 2024 lifted sales to x0.95 (vs baseline), and a 10% off in 2026 lifted to x1.56, but those were lower than the current price increase. The noise-adjusted uplift for promotions is x1.36, but this is a price increase, not a discount. A competitor opening across the street is a known demand-lowering driver. Past price increases (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) saw sales drop to 195 and 119, both below baseline. The 5.1% price hike likely suppresses demand. The noise-adjusted effect of price increases is not well-documented, but recent spikes in price without promotions caused a 28% drop. The competitor entry is a new, untested risk. Evidence is thin but consistent. Shrink toward 1.0. A price increase and new competitor reduce demand. No promotion or event to offset it.

brief:
PRODUCT: Whole Milk 1 gal | category Dairy | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.3 - 290.5 | 10%-90%: 156.2 - 281.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
